Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this selected complete logo with restrained optical refinement ONLY. Keep its flat blue bracket + central solid rounded rectangle + right two-piece sky-blue/blue i structure. Keep the straight horizontal cut in the right column.

CHANGE 1 — EQUAL PERCEIVED SPACING: The input has an overly narrow center-to-right gap and overly narrow bottom clearance. Open those up. Make all nearest-edge clearances read as one consistent approximately 28–30px channel at this 1254px canvas scale: left bracket to center; center to right column; top arm to both internal shapes; bottom arm to both internal shapes; the horizontal slit between the right cap and body. Top and bottom alignment of the two columns must match. At the upper-left and lower-left curved interface between bracket and central shape, adjust the bracket's INSIDE corners into smooth offset curves of the central rounded rectangle so the channel maintains the same apparent thickness through the turn, rather than flaring into triangular wedges or pinching. The left inner frame curve and facing central curve should be concentric/parallel where they face each other. Use optical compensation, not blindly identical numeric spacing. Maintain comfortable flowing negative space throughout.

CHANGE 2 — SLIGHTLY SMALLER CORNER RADII: Reduce the large corner radii of the central rounded rectangle and the right column's outer top and bottom ends by only about 15–20 percent, giving them slightly flatter crowns and longer straight sections while retaining their full, soft, rounded character. The center should still look like a tall softly rounded rectangle, not a sharp box. Right sky-blue cap stays short and full-width, lower blue body stays longer and full-width; together they look like one rounded rectangle split horizontally. The facing cut edges stay STRAIGHT, with discreet small fillets at their endpoints, also slightly reduced and smooth. Keep curvature and tangent transitions optically related across the three internal pieces, do not assign every corner the same radius mechanically.

GEOMETRY GUIDANCE ONLY: Keep the exterior bracket and overall canvas framing fixed. With the existing inner top arm around y=365 and bottom arm around y=947, internal shapes can run roughly y=395 to y=917. Left inner stem around x=454, central shape roughly x=484 to746, right column roughly x=776 to1014. Right slit roughly y=573 to603. These are only approximate anchors to equalize the gaps; optical fit takes priority. Adjust only the bracket inner corner contours if needed for uniform curved channels. Preserve the exterior broad upper-left sweep, top/bottom arm lengths, characteristic round projecting bottom-left toe.

PRESERVE: Original blue and sky-blue fills, general proportions, four filled components, simple flat treatment. No typography, new symbols, extra holes, bent cut, outline, glow, shadows, bevel, gradients added, or restyling. Smooth clean antialiased contours and fully transparent background and gaps, free of colored residual speckles. Output ONE complete square logo at the same framing as the reference, not a comparison sheet.

Precise logo refinement. Image 1 is the user's SELECTED original flat logo and authoritative design. Image 2 is a rejected refinement: its corners became TOO SQUARE and its left internal gap became TOO WIDE. Make a careful corrected edit of IMAGE 1, not a redesign.

Keep image 1's external bracket silhouette, canvas placement, blue color, sky-blue cap, relative sizes, and straight horizontal split i design. Change ONLY the spacing and a modest reduction in the interior shapes' corner radii.

Spacing: In image 1 widen the center-to-right vertical gap and the bottom horizontal gap to match the existing top and left gap, about 30 pixels in the source. Make the right cap-to-body straight horizontal slit the same perceived width. Top and bottom clearances equal, both columns aligned. Crucially the curved channel running between the left bracket and center should stay visually the same thickness through upper and lower turns: form the bracket inner corners as smooth offsets of the center corners. Do not widen the left gap like image 2. Do not merely space bounding boxes; balance the actual perceived transparent channels.

Corners: Start from image 1's very round capsule ends and reduce radii ONLY SLIGHTLY, around 10–15%. Retain noticeably round, full ends with only SHORT new flat top/bottom sections. The long horizontal flat crowns in image 2 are excessive and must not be copied. The center's top and bottom curves should be between image 1 and image 2 but much closer to image 1. The right cap outer top and lower body's bottom use the same perceived curvature family. Keep tiny soft end fillets on the flat split edges. The i upper cap must remain a domed cap, never a mostly rectangular tile.

Exact flat graphic style of image 1, no glow or shadow or outline, no new details. Clean smooth edges. Genuine transparent canvas and all gaps. Complete square logo only, no text or comparison.

Make an extremely small geometric correction to this logo. Preserve its present colors, shape design, corner radii, canvas and all outer contours.
1. Move BOTH parts of the right-hand i together to the LEFT by about 14 pixels in this 1254-pixel source. Do not shrink them, do not change their slit or their outlines. This should reduce the currently too-wide gap between the middle rectangle and right i from roughly 44px to roughly 30px, matching the 28–30px gap on the left.
2. Raise the bottom edge of the central rounded rectangle and of the right lower body by roughly 5px, preserving rounded profiles, so the bottom clearance above the blue horizontal base matches the top clearance. Keep their top positions fixed. Both bottoms must stay aligned.
3. All clearances should now visually match: left vertical channel, center-to-right vertical channel, top clearances, bottom clearances, right horizontal slit. Smooth the left bracket's inside rounded transitions ONLY if needed for equal apparent channel thickness around the center corners.
This is a final micro-adjustment, NOT a redesign. Keep the current slightly smaller radii, full-width sky-blue cap, blue lower body, and flat straight slit. No glow, no texture, no extra parts, no outline. Real fully transparent gaps and background, clean antialiasing and no color residue in empty space. One complete square logo.
